races.name: Coral Kincsem Heritage Handicap

runners_data.name: Bourbon Blues
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with strong Goodwood form (placed twice over 9-10f here), steps up to 10f on a course he handles well; Brian Meehan yard at 1/10 in the 14-day window is a concern, and he needs a gap to open from the rear that this race shape may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Bourbon Blues nonetheless catches the eye as the top-rated runner in a field of 14, and experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; third and second two and one runs back respectively suggest he retains ability, and 26 days between runs leaves him fresh.

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who can dictate entirely on his own terms; Charlie Johnston's yard is relatively quiet at 3/43 but David Egan knows him well, and his one course win came over this exact trip — his style-fit flag notes he is racing slightly out of role as a prominent type elevated to lead, but here that elevation works in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Evanesco landed a win three starts back and returns in good order on 20 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour — the risk is that two modest efforts since that success, including a fifth last time out, must be overcome.

runners_data.name: Harmonics
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden yard firing at 7/19 over 14 days, and Shane Foley comes over with obvious confidence; two recent wins including a Goodwood victory suggest he handles this course and ground, and his prominent style is perfectly suited to settling just off Evanesco's controlled fractions.
runners_data.comment: Harmonics has back-to-back wins two and three starts back to his name, but he managed only eighth last time out and arrives 40 days later needing to bounce back; he has run over today's trip before and draws stall three carrying 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Gonna Fly
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 3yo has won twice this season including over Goodwood's track, and Hector Crouch keeps the ride; the dip to 10f from a 10f placing here last time is not a concern, and a prominent pitch will suit, though the yard's 7/47 14-day strike rate is modest.
runners_data.comment: Gonna Fly won two starts back but was fifth last time out, and his distance-and-going experience is a plus; 130 lb from stall eleven is no small ask, however, and he'll need to bounce back sharply to make his presence felt here.

runners_data.name: Savvy Disko
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins have propelled him to an OR of 94, and Billy Loughnane's aggressive style will help him grab a prominent position early; the step up to 10f is new but his recent Goodwood win suggests he is a track specialist, and the S Woods yard at 0/9 recently is a mild flag.
runners_data.comment: Savvy Disko won his last two starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but a 33-day absence and a stiff 129 lb from stall 12 are factors to weigh against that encouragingly consistent recent form.

runners_data.name: Decade Of Time
runners_data.note: Won twice this season including over 10f at Goodwood, making him well-matched to this course and distance; Tom Marquand is a top-class booking and the horse consistently performs prominently, sitting just off the pace in a way that suits the expected tempo — Jack Channon at 4/19 is workmanlike.
runners_data.comment: Decade Of Time landed back-to-back wins in his last four starts before a runner-up effort most recently, so the recent form reads well, but a ranking of tenth in this field and 129 lb to carry are significant asks.

runners_data.name: Birgham Dub
runners_data.note: Won over 12f at Sandown and 7f at Goodwood, making this 10f something of an unknown trip; Oisin Murphy is always a strong positive and Jane Chapple-Hyam's 2/10 recent rate is decent, but the 42-day absence and that last run of 0/12f here last time temper enthusiasm despite his prominent style.
runners_data.comment: Showed his best with back-to-back wins in recent starts but has been unplaced last time out, and 42 days off adds a fitness query; has experience of today's going, though our rating of 98 suggests there's ability to tap into from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Lion of Alba
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's colt is a genuine front-runner by nature but, with the field packed with prominent types, he is unlikely to secure his preferred position and has been mapped to midfield accordingly; his recent form is modest (7th, 4th, 7th in last three), and the tongue-tie is noted, but the style displacement here materially reduces his chance of landing the race on his own terms.
runners_data.comment: Lion of Alba's win four starts back and his experience on today's going make him a legitimate threat here, and 21 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; the risk is that he's been out of the first three in his last three starts.

runners_data.name: Dial Me In
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's yard is in excellent form at 16/67, and Dylan Browne McMonagle is a major positive booking with a big-race temperament; however, this horse is a true prominent runner who struggled to 13th over 12f at Goodwood last time, and being forced into midfield against his nature (tongue-tie fitted) makes his task significantly harder than his raw ability suggests.
runners_data.comment: Dial Me In shaped well when second two starts back and has previous experience over today's trip and going, while a trainer firing at 28% makes him a serious contender from stall 4; the worry is that last-time-out unplaced run leaves something to prove on current form.

runners_data.name: Dark Whisper
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three starts and improving rapidly, Dark Whisper is Jamie Spencer's mount for David Menuisier whose yard has gone cold at 0/12; a genuine prominent runner who will be squeezed for position here, the redistribution into midfield is a real tactical problem given Spencer's preference for patient rides, creating an awkward mismatch of horse instinct and jockey style.
runners_data.comment: Dark Whisper arrives here rated bottom two of 14 on our figures and ranked 13th overall, making him hard to fancy despite a win last time out; his experience on today's going is the one genuine foothold to cling to.

runners_data.name: Strength Of Spirit
runners_data.note: Karl Burke's yard is active and in form at 10/33, but Strength Of Spirit's recent record at Goodwood is patchy — four runs on the course producing only modest positions; pushed into midfield despite preferring to race prominently, this horse has been in and out of form (138934 string) and the combination of style displacement and inconsistency make it hard to make a case.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back but has struggled for consistency, with a ninth and a fourth in between suggesting he blows hot and cold; has run over today's going before, carries 121 lb from stall 10, and a trainer firing at 34% offers encouragement.

runners_data.name: Ciarrai Abu
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's progressive 3yo has won twice at Goodwood at 8f and is stepping up to 10f for the first time; George Wood takes the ride and the 3/12 14-day trainer return is solid, but the unknown trip, a field where he cannot secure his natural prominent position, and having to race in midfield against his instincts all combine to make his task tough despite his obvious course aptitude.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, Ciarrai Abu is hard to fancy despite winning last time out and a second win three starts back; the fourth-placed effort two starts back and a sixth five starts back temper enthusiasm, and his speed rating of 78 leaves him well short of the top-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Loz Vegas
runners_data.note: Peter Chapple-Hyam's hold-up runner has not won in seven starts and his recent form string reads 58-654; Marco Ghiani will be patient from the rear but this horse needs things to fall perfectly in a race where the pace is likely to be controlled, and the yard at 0/5 in 14 days offers no trainer angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than fourth, Loz Vegas faces a stiff task from stall six off 120 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 92 hints at some unexploited ability.

runners_data.name: Lean d'Aislingean
runners_data.note: Charlie Pike's lightly-raced 3yo has only three starts to her name and the form figures of 932 are uninspiring; Edward Greatrex is a competent booking, but a horse with no wins, questionable Goodwood form, and who comes from the back in a race favouring prominent types looks to need a very specific and unlikely scenario to be involved.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Lean d'Aislingean faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's going before and those placings on his last two starts show some ability, but the gulf to the top-rated runners looks significant from stall one.

races.paceDynamic: Evanesco is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure expected at the head of affairs, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f at Goodwood. Behind him, Harmonics, Gonna Fly, Savvy Disko, Decade Of Time, and Birgham Dub all carry prominent-style profiles, but with so many competing for those forward berths, the field is heavily congested in the top half — several will be unable to hold their natural position. Lion of Alba, Dial Me In, Dark Whisper, Strength Of Spirit, and Ciarrai Abu are all true prominent types redistributed into the midfield map because they simply cannot all race where they want; the horses most likely to actually secure a prominent pitch are Harmonics and Savvy Disko, who have the tactical speed and class to push forward early. The result is an evenly-paced first half that gradually quickens into the straight, with Evanesco controlling the tempo and the midfield becoming compressed — closers will face a wall of horses, meaning genuine hold-up runners will struggle to find daylight. This race shape strongly favours horses able to race prominently just off the controlled leader, giving them first run into the Goodwood straight without burning early petrol.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Evanesco Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Evanesco dictates a measured gallop and the race only quickens in the final two furlongs, allowing horses racing second or third to pounce.
scenarios.body: Evanesco sets a sustainable fractions-based tempo and the race develops into a straightforward prominent-runner's contest in the home straight; horses settled just behind the leader get first run and first access to fresh ground. Harmonics and Savvy Disko are ideally positioned to capitalise, with their recent winning form on similar going underwriting their claims.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the field fails to coordinate a challenge and the compressed midfield leaves no horse with a clean run to close, allowing Evanesco to steal it.
scenarios.body: The congested group of prominent types fail to organise behind Evanesco, with none able to pick off the leader cleanly as rivals block each other's runs into the short Goodwood straight. Evanesco's recent winning form over the course and distance and his uncontested lead prove decisive, and he simply outstays a disorganised finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surges Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is surprisingly brisk, burning off the prominent pack and opening a gap for a well-timed late run from further back.
scenarios.body: A slightly hotter tempo than expected from multiple jockeys trying to grab position depletes the leaders' reserves, and a runner coming from off the pace finds a lane in the final furlong. Bourbon Blues, stepping up in trip on a course where he has shown ability, is the natural candidate from hold-up in this shape; Lean d'Aislingean has the profile if the race truly falls apart.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the true prominent horses shuffled into midfield defies their mapped position and fights through to land the race from an unexpected angle.
scenarios.body: Lion of Alba or Dial Me In forces their way forward early despite the traffic, secures a pitch they were always wanting and proves the pace map underestimated their resolution; Dial Me In in particular has the class for the trip and Joseph O'Brien's stable is in good form. However, the style-fit discount and the crowded early stages make this genuinely the least likely outcome, dependent on fortune as much as ability.

watchPoints.text: Lion of Alba, Dial Me In, Dark Whisper, Strength Of Spirit, and Ciarrai Abu are all natural prominent types who cannot all get their position — watch the first two furlongs for crowding and potential trouble as these horses compete for the same stretch of real estate behind Evanesco.

Evanesco holds a [STYLE_FIT=0.93] flag as a prominent horse elevated to lead — if he jumps slowly or is reluctant to go forward, the entire pace map collapses and the race becomes a tactical mess with no true pacer.

Birgham Dub has been off 42 days and his last Goodwood run was a tailed-off 10th over 12f — watch for Oisin Murphy trying to aggressively reclaim a prominent pitch on a horse that may not be fully wound up.

Harmonics and Savvy Disko have both won at Goodwood recently and both want prominent positions — if they go head-to-head for the same ground early, the one who settles second will likely be fresher turning in and should be watched in the straight.

Bourbon Blues is the most interesting hold-up runner in a race that does not obviously suit closers — watch whether Joe Leavy attempts to angle him wider early to get a clear run, as any sign of that manoeuvre suggests the team expects the midfield to be very congested.

races.name: Markel Richmond Stakes (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Adaay of Scarlett
runners_data.note: Has run all five career starts at Goodwood on similar going, recording five runs of at least placed form including two wins; a natural prominent racer under Oisin Murphy who should secure a clean position just off Jaan Ki Tukri's back and is proven around this exact track.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in fine recent fettle, Adaay of Scarlett has finished second in each of his last three starts after back-to-back wins, showing he retains ability; with experience of today's trip and going and 21 days fresh, he rates the one to beat from stall two.

runners_data.name: Big Cigar
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D last time and is trained by Fahey who fires 1/40 in a 14-day window; thrives racing up with the pace, but with the prominent berths already oversubscribed he is likely to find himself a slot or two further back than ideal, which tempers expectations.|
runners_data.comment: Big Cigar won last time out and has run over today's trip, but that fifth two starts back is a blot on an otherwise solid recent record; 128 lb from stall seven is the challenge facing him here.

runners_data.name: Cut A Dash
runners_data.note: Hannon's runner was beaten into fourth here over 6f last time before that course win over 5f, so the step back up to this trip at Goodwood needs to prove itself; races prominently under Levey and a 44-day break is worth monitoring, though the trainer maintains a solid 9/49 recent strike-rate.|
runners_data.comment: Cut A Dash won two starts back and returns on familiar distance and going terms, with our rating of 105 marking him out as a leading threat from stall 8; the main concern is whether 44 days off has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Flann Sunna
runners_data.note: Won her first two starts both over 6f at Goodwood, giving her excellent course and distance form under Buick; her natural race style is prominent, but with the pace slots filled she has been shuffled toward the rear of the map — she will need Buick to find the clearest route home from an uncharacteristic position.|
runners_data.comment: Flann Sunna rates below the field on our figures despite back-to-back wins in his last two starts, and that speed rating of 69 gives little encouragement against stronger company here; he has run over today's trip and comes in fresh enough at 20 days, but it is hard to get enthusiastic from stall 10 carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Hickory Lad
runners_data.note: Five career runs have produced a mix of wins and placed efforts on Good ground, and his three visits to Goodwood include a 6f placed run last time; like Flann Sunna he has been pushed back on the map from his natural attacking position and Sam James will need to find daylight late.|
runners_data.comment: Hickory Lad arrives in fine recent trim — a winner two starts back and third last time out, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour at 128 lb from stall nine; the main risk is whether that weight anchors him late.

runners_data.name: Jaan Ki Tukri
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field; wore a hood last time and won over this C&D 16 days ago, so conditions and track could not suit better — the key question is whether the prominent cluster applies early pressure that destabilises his rhythm.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of ten on our figures and his speed rating lags behind the principals, making him hard to fancy at the weights despite carrying 128 lb from stall five. That recent win offers some hope, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Man's Best Friend
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner in the field at OR 120, winning over this course and distance last time for Ryan Moore and Aidan O'Brien; only eight days since that run which is tight but the team clearly has him cherry-ripe, and Moore's ability to take a prominent position without burning the engine is the dominant tactical asset in this race.|
runners_data.comment: Rated lowest in the field and his speed figure of 66 gives little encouragement, though he does bring a win eight days ago and experience of today's trip and conditions — hard to fancy against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Mr Macartney
runners_data.note: Wore a visor here and has a modest recent form string of 41767; naturally wants to race up front but finds himself displaced into midfield by the volume of pace — his OR of 91 represents the lowest rating in the field and the style mismatch compounds that gap.|
runners_data.comment: Mr Macartney showed what he's capable of with a win four starts back, but three subsequent finishes of seventh, seventh and sixth suggest he's in a difficult patch; has run over today's trip and going before, and 40 days off could freshen him up.

runners_data.name: Night In Vegas
runners_data.note: Two course wins including one on Good to Firm ground, so the going and track hold no fears for Eve Johnson Houghton's filly; 44 days since her last run is the main question mark, though she is a genuine prominent type who should secure a position just behind the lead if the scrimmage for berths allows.|
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins boost his claims, though he's been off 44 days and drops marginally below the official mark on our rating; has run over today's trip and going, and stall three is his draw from 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Where Love Lives
runners_data.note: Two wins from three starts for Donnacha O'Brien, the last over 5f on this going; her trainer has zero winners from 14 runners in the past fortnight and the horse herself will be squeezed out of her preferred prominent slot — she will be doing her best work from further back than suits.|
runners_data.comment: Where Love Lives won two of his last three starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a serious contender from stall one carrying 128 lb — the concern is that unplaced effort on his most recent outing needs excusing.

races.paceDynamic: Jaan Ki Tukri is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger for the lead, should stride into an uncontested gallop from the gates, controlling tempo through the first two furlongs on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood. The prominent ranks are heavily congested — Adaay of Scarlett, Cut A Dash, Man's Best Friend, and Night In Vegas all want to race close to the pace, creating a genuine battle for position between the 2f and 3f marks that could tighten up the group racing up the straight. Big Cigar, Where Love Lives, and Mr Macartney are all naturally prominent types who have been displaced to midfield by the sheer volume of pace in this field, meaning they will race out of their preferred position and face traffic as the field fans out. This shape overwhelmingly favours horses that can track Jaan Ki Tukri from a close-up, racing-prominent berth and quicken off a genuine but controlled pace — true hold-up runners are absent in any meaningful sense, and the displaced midfielders carry a real positional disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jaan Ki Tukri Dictates, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Jaan Ki Tukri leads uncontested and sets a fair-to-honest Good to Firm gallop, inviting the closestprominent chasers to challenge from 2f out.
scenarios.body: The front-runner controls tempo without being harried, allowing riders like Ryan Moore (Man's Best Friend) and Oisin Murphy (Adaay of Scarlett) to position perfectly just off the pace and unleash a sustained run through the final furlong; the Goodwood straight rewards horses travelling smoothly in the slipstream.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Burns Off Field
scenarios.trigger: If the congested prominent group hustles Jaan Ki Tukri into a searingly fast early gallop that decimates those up with the pace.
scenarios.body: A hot early pace on Good to Firm ground leaves the front-runners and prominents flattening out inside the final furlong, handing an advantage to any horse that has been able to switch off slightly further back; Hickory Lad and Flann Sunna, though mapped wide of their natural position, would be best-placed of the rear-end runners if the race truly falls apart.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Gaps Close
scenarios.trigger: If the four-wide prominent cluster causes significant interference 2-3f out, causing checks and switches that disrupt the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Traffic chaos in the middle stages nullifies the positional advantage of the closer chasers and leaves the outcome to whoever emerges cleanest from trouble; Man's Best Friend with Ryan Moore's course craft and Cut A Dash with Sean Levey's local knowledge are best equipped to navigate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Displaced Midfielders Steal Through
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine pace-setters fade abruptly and Big Cigar or Where Love Lives thread through from their unnatural midfield berth to claim a late prize.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because Big Cigar and Where Love Lives are racing well out of their preferred prominent roles and would need a rare set of circumstances — a truly punishing early pace plus a clear late passage — to strike; their style-fit discounts make this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Man's Best Friend is the class act in the race and Ryan Moore will aim to slot into the prime position just off Jaan Ki Tukri — if he secures that berth unimpeded at the 4f mark, the race is likely over by the 1f pole.

The congested prominent group — Adaay of Scarlett, Cut A Dash, Night In Vegas, and Man's Best Friend — creates a real risk of crowding and checking between the 3f and 2f marks on the Goodwood straight; watch for any horse taken wide or squeezed on the rail.

Jaan Ki Tukri won over this course and distance 16 days ago and sets the pace alone, but if the chasing pack ignores the solo leader and applies early pressure through the first furlong, his controlled gallop could accelerate into something more destructive for his own chance.

Flann Sunna and Hickory Lad are both natural front-end types shuffled toward the rear by the busy pace map; William Buick on Flann Sunna in particular will need to find a clean passage through — if traffic clears she could dramatically outrun her mapped position.

Big Cigar's C&D win last time is the obvious form flag, but Oisin Orr will need to improvise a prominent position from a congested early order — monitor how quickly he can establish himself in the first two furlongs.

races.name: Maison Perrier Gordon Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Geryon
runners_data.note: Won over course and distance at Goodwood last time, Colin Keane takes over, and his sim-going record of 7 runs on similar surfaces is solid — a genuine prominent racer who should slot in directly behind Venetian Lace in his natural position, making him ideally placed under this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Geryon is the one to beat here — a winner last time out, with a second three starts back, he returns on going he has encountered before and has the highest rating in the field. The 132 lb burden is the one thing to watch.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Brilliance
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's lightly-raced colt posted a 1m2f Goodwood win last month and drops slightly in trip here, with Hector Crouch riding; handles good ground adequately but limited sim-going exposure (2/6) is worth noting alongside a soft-ground heavy form pattern earlier this season.
runners_data.comment: Bay Of Brilliance posted back-to-back wins three and four starts back and returns here fresh enough on 25 days' rest, having run over today's trip before. The main risk is his unplaced effort last time out, which must be answered.

runners_data.name: Enceladus
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's unbeaten-in-two horse is in excellent current form, but his natural prominent style has been displaced to midfield in the map because the field is crowded with pace-committed types — McMonagle will likely need to work harder than ideal to obtain a forward pitch, which tempers the shape-fit.
runners_data.comment: Enceladus has won his last two starts, but our rating ranks him sixth of seven here, and his speed figure of 86 leaves him needing significant improvement. Third three starts back and fourth starts back add some consistency, though he faces a stiff task on these assessments.

runners_data.name: Magnetude
runners_data.note: Won at Goodwood over this trip on his penultimate start and clearly handles course and distance well; Oisin Murphy is a booking that commands respect, though the horse's natural prominence means he too is mapped away from his preferred slot, and his style-fit score reflects that positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of seven on our figures and his speed rating of 83 trails the field, making him hard to fancy despite an eighth two starts back sandwiched between better efforts — though he has winning form in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Sahara King
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's colt has placed twice over 1m2f on good-to-firm-adjacent ground, but the redistribution to the rear is the furthest from his natural game — he is a prominent-minded horse who will find it hardest of all to execute the hold-up role shown on the map, and James Doyle will need to adapt tactically.
runners_data.comment: Sahara King was unplaced last time out after consecutive second-place finishes two and three starts back, and a winner five starts back, so the form is mixed. Familiarity with today's going helps, but 40 days off and 129 lb make this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Shaihaan
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's yard is 0/14 in the last 14 days, adding a trainer flag to an already complicated positional picture; a naturally prominent operator shuffled back by a congested pace profile, he showed a win at 1m2f on good ground at The Curragh but has finished off the pace in both Goodwood runs.
runners_data.comment: Shaihaan brings solid recent form to the table — third two starts back and a winner four starts back — and he has experience of both today's trip and going conditions; his rating of 109 underlines his claims. The fifth last time out is the one to forgive.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lace
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's filly is the lone confirmed front-runner who will lead by default, but her best form reads 8f-9f and her two runs at 1m4f include a soft-ground ninth; on good-to-firm at Goodwood over this extended trip, stamina under a solo lead is a fair question, even at a sustainable gallop.
runners_data.comment: Venetian Lace showed sharp ability when second and third in consecutive starts, and her experience on today's going is a clear asset carrying 126 lb; the risk is that two subsequent below-par efforts — seventh and ninth in her last two — leave her needing to bounce back sharply.

races.paceDynamic: Venetian Lace is the sole confirmed front-runner in a seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival to challenge for the lead, she will dictate terms at a measured, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over 1m4f at Goodwood. The pace is unlikely to be pressured, meaning the race will be run at a rhythm that suits those travelling comfortably just off the leader rather than those needing a truly searching test to bring their finishing kick into play. Shaihaan, Enceladus, and Magnetude are all natural prominent types who have been displaced to midfield in the map because there is simply insufficient space at the front for all of them — Geryon and Bay Of Brilliance, with their form profile and jockey bookings, are best placed to actually secure the prominent berths directly behind Venetian Lace. This race shape — a controlled, single-pacemaker scenario with a compacted field — strongly favours horses racing prominently in the first two or three, where they can dictate their own rhythm and pounce without needing a long-range run from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Venetian Lace Controls, Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Venetian Lace sets an uncontested lead and the two genuine prominent types slot in close behind from the outset.
scenarios.body: Venetian Lace rolls along at a fair but manageable clip, and the horses travelling just off her have first run turning into the straight; on good-to-firm Goodwood where positional advantage from the home turn is crucial, those who have been racing in the first three have a decisive edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Strong Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Venetian Lace crawls and the race becomes a sprint for home, favouring the horse with the most raw class and acceleration.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow early gallop compresses the field and sets up a furious final quarter-mile where class and a well-timed challenge from a midfield position proves decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Force Muddled Pace
scenarios.trigger: If multiple redistributed prominent horses push forward and create a more genuinely contested early pace than the map suggests.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected early tempo stretches the field and puts Venetian Lace under pressure sooner than she would like, bringing stamina to the fore in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Runs Through Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and a late-challenging type picks off the fading leaders in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With the prominent horses having emptied their tanks in a contested race, a horse allowed to settle and come from off the pace cuts through late; Sahara King, though mapped at the rear out of natural role, could benefit if all the stars align.

watchPoints.text: Venetian Lace's stamina at 1m4f on good-to-firm must be monitored — if she ties up in the final quarter-mile, the race opens dramatically for those just behind her.

Shaihaan, Enceladus, and Magnetude are all prominent types who may press forward early despite the map showing them in midfield — watch for a busier-than-expected opening half-mile if multiple riders try to reclaim their natural position.

Geryon's last three runs at Goodwood include two fourths, suggesting course form is mixed despite the distance win — Colin Keane will need to judge the pace perfectly to convert prominent positioning into victory.

Bay Of Brilliance's two most recent runs came on soft ground and his only good-ground run at Goodwood was a second over 1m2f — the step up to 1m4f on quicker ground is the key unknown for Ralph Beckett's colt today.

Trainer 14-day strike rates are subdued across the board — Johnston (3/43), G M Lyons (4/25), and O'Brien (0/14) — meaning in-form yard momentum is not a tailwind for the most likely pace-setters in this race.

races.name: Qatar Nassau Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Friendly Soul
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's five-year-old has won three of her last five starts and returns to Goodwood, where she has form; 43 days off is not a concern for this yard and Good to Firm suits, but her 8f and soft-ground form slightly clouds her profile at 10f on a quick surface.
runners_data.comment: Friendly Soul has won three of her last five starts, with a victory three starts back, and has experience of today's trip and going — she shapes as a leading danger. The pull-up two starts back is the one flag to note.

runners_data.name: See The Fire
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's mare has won twice at Goodwood over this exact trip and arrives as the only dedicated front-runner in the field; her STYLE_FIT flag notes she could be pushed into a sharper lead role than ideal in Group 1 company, but her course-and-distance record makes her the pace architect regardless.
runners_data.comment: See The Fire has back-to-back wins in her recent starts and has run over today's trip and going, making her the one to beat here; she carries 135 lb from stall one, and the 43-day gap is the only question mark against a mare who profiles strongly at the top of this field.

runners_data.name: Botagoz
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's three-year-old is a natural up-with-the-pace filly whose two wins this season came on Flat, Standard and Good ground at shorter trips; she wants to race prominently but with Diamond Necklace and Friendly Soul also forward-going, she is almost certain to find herself further back than Varian would prefer, racing in a role that blunts her style.
runners_data.comment: Botagoz arrives on the back of three wins in her last four starts, with the sole blemish a third two runs back, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — the main question is whether 126 lb blunts her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Diamond Necklace
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's unbeaten five-from-five filly is the most imposing form entrant in the field and Ryan Moore will attempt to manufacture a prominent pitch rather than accept a midfield slot; her three wins at 10f show she handles the step up, though she has yet to race on going this quick and that is a small query at Goodwood.
runners_data.comment: Five wins in her last five starts make Diamond Necklace impossible to dismiss lightly, and she has going experience in her favour — but our figures rank her last of five in this field, and the 46-day absence adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Moments Of Joy
runners_data.note: The stable second-string for O'Brien has the worst recent form in the race, with a run of 6-4-0 at the top level, and her genuine hold-up profile makes her entirely dependent on a strongly-run race that this small five-runner field is unlikely to provide; Good to Firm is not a concern, but class and pace scenario are.
runners_data.comment: Moments Of Joy showed genuine promise with a second in her last five starts, and has experience over today's trip and conditions — the worry is she's been winless in recent starts and returns after a 46-day absence.

races.paceDynamic: See The Fire is the lone confirmed front-runner and, in a five-runner Group 1 field, should be able to stride into an uncontested lead from the outset, setting a honest but controlled gallop on Good to Firm ground over ten furlongs. Friendly Soul will press from a prominent berth and is the only horse likely to genuinely sit at See The Fire's quarters, meaning the pace is real but not chaotic. Diamond Necklace and Botagoz are both natural prominent types who will find themselves shuffled into a midfield role they do not naturally want, as there is simply not enough room for three horses to sit in the first two; Ryan Moore's mount is the more likely of the two to manufacture a forward position given Moore's tactical authority, but neither can guarantee their preferred slot. This race shape — a clear, metronomic gallop set by a single front-runner with one horse pressing — classically favours a prominent or close-tracking runner who can travel into the pace without burning fuel, rather than a genuine hold-up horse forced to make ground from an unfamiliar deep position; Moments Of Joy, with the worst recent form in the field and a true hold-up profile, is the profile most at odds with what this shape serves up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: See The Fire Controls
scenarios.trigger: If See The Fire leads unmolested and Friendly Soul settles in behind without applying undue pressure, creating a smooth, even-tempo race.
scenarios.body: See The Fire dictates every yard on the Good to Firm ground, conserving energy through the long Goodwood bend before quickening from two furlongs out; a horse that has already won twice at Goodwood over this trip is perfectly suited. Friendly Soul, tracking in second throughout, is ideally placed to pounce if the leader ties up, but risks being beaten for a change of gear if See The Fire's recent Group 1 form translates here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If See The Fire's pace is just strong enough to stretch the field but leaves enough for a close-tracking horse to reel it in over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Diamond Necklace, if Moore can find a prominent position from the widest draw, would travel powerfully into the race and use her unbeaten record to deliver a sustained challenge; her five consecutive wins show she handles any pace scenario. Botagoz, also a natural close-up runner who has won two of her last three, could benefit if the pace scenario suits a horse travelling just off the principals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out, creating enough of a test to leave front-runners and prominent horses vulnerable in the final 150 yards.
scenarios.body: This shape would in theory suit Moments Of Joy making up ground from the back, but her recent form (0-6-4) gives little confidence that she has the quality to capitalise even if the race falls perfectly. The scenario requires See The Fire to tie up and Friendly Soul to also fade, which demands a pace level this small field is unlikely to generate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If runners are cautious early in the small field, creating a falsely-run race that collapses into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A lack of early commitment could neutralise See The Fire's front-running advantage and turn the race into a scramble from two furlongs out, which would bring Diamond Necklace's pure acceleration to the fore. Botagoz, who won over shorter on Good ground at Goodwood, would also have claims in a speed-dominated finish, though both face the uncertainty of having been pushed out of their natural position.

watchPoints.text: See The Fire — watch whether Oisin Murphy is pressed into going faster than intended if Diamond Necklace and Friendly Soul both try to secure prominent positions in the early stages; any increase in early tempo could compromise her staying power.

Diamond Necklace — Ryan Moore will attempt to push forward from stall five; watch the first furlong to see if she secures a prominent berth or is forced to settle mid-pack, as the latter materially changes her chance.

Botagoz — Ray Dawson faces a genuine tactical problem with three prominent-profile horses in five runners; if she cannot land a forward pitch, her form profile loses much of its relevance in a race where she will be racing out of style.

Moments Of Joy — watch her market move; if she drifts significantly in the ring it confirms she is regarded as a remote outsider even by connections, which would align with the form evidence and a race shape that offers her nothing.
Friendly Soul — 43 days since last run for Gosden; watch paddock behaviour and early market activity as a fitness indicator, given she has not been seen since a mid-June run at this track.

races.name: Buccellati Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Schrodinger's Cat
runners_data.note: Confirmed sole front-runner with back-to-back Goodwood 5f wins including a course victory; uncontested lead on Good to Firm is a major asset but the field will be tight early and an 18-runner draw could be disruptive — STYLE_FIT flag notes style out of role but here the lead is genuine.|
runners_data.comment: Schrodinger's Cat won three starts back and was second two starts back, showing consistent form at this level, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the main concern is that sixth last time out suggests he may not be fully wound up again just yet.

runners_data.name: Baker Blue
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a course win at Goodwood 5f to his name (STA) and improving form; Pat Dobbs is a useful course jockey, but only 8/14 runs in similar going and closing at Goodwood over 5f requires a strong pace to materialise.|
runners_data.comment: Baker Blue shaped well when runner-up last time out, and has experience of both today's trip and conditions — he arrives fit on a 13-day turnaround carrying 135 lb from stall 13. The main risk is his trainer's current form at just 1 from 22 over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Naana's Shadow
runners_data.note: Three wins from five Goodwood 5f starts in similar going makes this a standout course-and-distance profile; Oisin Murphy in the saddle and a trainer in excellent current form (1/8 T14) — natural prominent style suits this race shape well.|
runners_data.comment: Naana's Shadow won three of her last six starts, including back-to-back victories two and three starts back, but she was beaten into ninth last time out and faces a stiff task from a our rating of 93 ranked sixth of eighteen; has run over today's trip and going, and 19 days off looks sharp enough.

runners_data.name: Manatee Mehmas
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope takes over for O'Meara's 3yo who won at Goodwood 5f and goes on similar ground; held up 33 days which is slightly longer since last run than ideal, but all four career runs at Goodwood 5f and a tidy prominent style represent solid credentials.|
runners_data.comment: Manatee Mehmas shaped with real promise when third last time out, and a winner four starts back, he has experience of today's trip and conditions — the main question is whether that eighth two starts back was a blip or a sign of inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Dazzling Haze
runners_data.note: Cowell's 3yo has three wins on Good or faster at 5f including two Goodwood victories; natural prominent style suits but the trainer is 0/13 in the last 14 days and a 41-day absence warrants slight caution.|
runners_data.comment: Dazzling Haze has run over today's trip and going, and her last-five form includes wins two and five starts back, but she was unplaced last time out and carries 131 lb from stall 16, making this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Miss Yechance
runners_data.note: Burke's charge has won at Goodwood 5f in similar going and K.R. Burke is a lively 10/33 in the last 14 days; prominent style fits the likely shape and the drop back from 7f last time could sharpen her.|
runners_data.comment: Second two starts back shows she can threaten at this level, but a seventh last time out after 41 days off is a concern; has run over today's trip and carries 130 lb from stall 6, leaving her a midfield proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Pilu
runners_data.note: Roger Teal runner whose recent form is at 6f — all five historical runs are at six furlongs, making this step down to 5f a genuine query; natural prominent style fits structurally but the trip shortening is a flag.|
runners_data.comment: Ran second two starts back but has disappointed either side of that effort, with a fifth last time out the latest concern; has run over today's trip and going, and 21 days between runs should leave him fresh, though 127 lb is no lightweight ask from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Shes Got A Brother
runners_data.note: Two course wins at 5f on soft and standard, but only 2/5 runs on Good or Firm ground in the historical record — the Good to Firm surface here is a mild concern for Easterby's 3yo despite a prominent style.|
runners_data.comment: Ran third two starts back and has won twice in her last five starts, with experience of today's trip and going in her favour. Returning after 40 days, she carries 127 lb from stall 14, but her overall profile makes her our pick here.

runners_data.name: River Spey
runners_data.note: A genuinely front-running type by nature, though the busy field means Ed Walker's 3yo is unlikely to secure that position and will need to settle for tracking; Kieran Shoemark rides well at Goodwood and two wins on this course at 6f are encouraging, but 5f on Good to Firm is unproven.|
runners_data.comment: River Spey has won twice in his last five starts — a winner two starts back and a winner four starts back — but he was unplaced last time out and faces a stiff test from stall 17 carrying 126 lb, despite his trainer firing at 28% lately.

runners_data.name: Old Is Gold
runners_data.note: James Doyle takes the ride on Balding's 3yo who hasn't run for 97 days — the extended absence is the biggest flag here; won at Goodwood 5f on similar ground but naturally front-running and racing in a congested midfield position is a structural challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back gives Old Is Gold a form line to work with, and the trainer's 26% strike rate over the past fortnight is worth noting, but he hasn't threatened since and returns after 97 days off — freshness cuts both ways at this level.

runners_data.name: One And Gone
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winners at Goodwood 5f and a natural early-pace horse; front-running instincts mean Ryan Kavanagh (3lb claim) will find it hard to slot into a tracking position with so many similar types, but the course form is the best in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 18 on our figures and 4 lb below his official mark, One And Gone faces a stiff ask here, though he arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has experience over today's trip and going; stall 12 is his draw, and 27 days off shouldn't be an issue.

runners_data.name: Quantum Power
runners_data.note: Three consecutive Goodwood 5f wins make this Tom Clover runner the most in-form horse at the course; wears a visor and David Egan takes over — natural prominent type who will be competing for position, but the course strike-rate is hard to ignore.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 18 on our figures, Quantum Power faces a stiff ask from stall 10 off 126 lb, and a speed rating of 74 leaves him well short of what's needed here — yet three wins in his last six starts, including his last three, show he arrives in career-best form.

runners_data.name: Kolkata Knight
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie; has a Goodwood 5f win on soft ground but only 7/9 on similar going and recent form shows an 8th and 11th at the course — hold-up style with Dascombe who has had a quiet recent spell (0/8 T14).|
runners_data.comment: Kolkata Knight showed his quality with a win and a second in recent starts, but a fourth and two poorer efforts since then cloud his profile; he has experience of today's distance and going, yet a 123 lb burden from stall 18 makes life harder.

runners_data.name: Noble Vow
runners_data.note: Hannon's 3yo hasn't run for 60 days and is a genuine prominent type by instinct, forced into midfield by race shape; won on soft and firm turf but Good to Firm at Goodwood 5f is unproven and the long absence adds risk.|
runners_data.comment: Noble Vow brings back-to-back wins two and three starts back into the reckoning, though he was unplaced last time out and returns after 60 days off; he has run over today's trip and going, and a mark of 82 leaves some room on our 88 rating.

runners_data.name: Call Margot
runners_data.comment: Call Margot showed a second two starts back but has otherwise struggled for consistency, finishing sixth last time out and ranking well down on our figures here. She has run over today's trip and going, and 120 lb from stall 3 is workable, but it's hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: U S S Charleston
runners_data.note: Ran just 6 days ago — the quick turnaround is the defining factor here for De Souza's 3yo; natural prominent type who couldn't get that position last time, and form figures of 391505 give little encouragement in this competitive field.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 16 of 18 on our figures, U S S Charleston makes a difficult case — fifth last time out and largely out of the frame in recent starts, his sole consolation a win four starts back. Has run over today's trip and going, and returns on a quick turnaround, but the form and ranking make him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Coyy
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's hold-up filly has two Goodwood 5f wins (2W4P on the course) and wears a tongue-tie; Saffie Osborne rides and the 9-day turnaround from a win last time gives freshness — hold-up style needs the pace to truly materialise.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 17 of 18 on our figures, Coyy is hard to fancy despite winning last time out nine days ago; he was fourth two starts back and seventh three starts back, and that inconsistency makes him difficult to trust, even granted his distance-and-going experience and a handy 117 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Truly Glamorous
runners_data.note: Two recent wins including at Goodwood 5f in Good conditions; wears a hood and Gina Mangan claims; hold-up style on a big field at 5f is viable if the early tempo is strong enough, and the improving profile from a low OR of 72 is noteworthy.|
runners_data.comment: Truly Glamorous ranks bottom of the field on our figures, and his speed rating offers little encouragement, though he does arrive on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going before — small consolations at best.

races.paceDynamic: Schrodinger's Cat is the one confirmed front-runner here, rated P with strong Goodwood course form at 5f and solid similar-going figures, and with no genuine challenger for the lead this horse should roll along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop rather than a true searching pace. With 18 runners over Goodwood's stiff 5f rise, the field is packed with prominent types — River Spey, Quantum Power, One And Gone, Noble Vow, and U S S Charleston are all natural early-pace horses who will be jostling for position in the first two furlongs, unable to all settle into their preferred spot. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can physically secure that ground: Quantum Power (three recent Goodwood 5f wins), One And Gone (back-to-back winners here), and River Spey are the three most likely to push through and press into prominent positions behind Schrodinger's Cat given their recent course form, despite being redistributed on the pace map. With sustainable fractions rather than a true test of stamina and a field forced into a bunched early order, the race shape favours horses who can travel prominently in the slipstream of the leader, pick up the Good to Firm surface quickly, and possess a sharp turn of foot in the final furlong — the tracking prominent profile has the structural edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Prominent Tracking
scenarios.trigger: If Schrodinger's Cat leads at a fair pace and the bunch behind it settles with prominent trackers ideally placed at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Schrodinger's Cat dictates a manageable tempo on Good to Firm ground, allowing horses that track in the first three or four to pounce with a clean run off the bend; the slight Goodwood rise filters out the hold-up brigade who are left too far back to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Scrap Early
scenarios.trigger: If the glut of natural prominent horses causes crowding and a faster-than-expected early tempo as several fight for position.
scenarios.body: The elevated early pace burns off Schrodinger's Cat and the natural front-markers, compressing the race into a sprint finish for the whole field; horses with a high cruising speed that can still quicken off a stronger gallop benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is high enough to string the field out and open a gap for genuine hold-up horses to pick up late ground.
scenarios.body: Baker Blue, Coyy, Truly Glamorous, and Call Margot would need the tempo to genuinely stretch the prominent horses; this is structurally possible but depends on pace contributors doing the donkey work at a racecourse where hold-up horses are often caught flat-footed at 5f.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Suits Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the mass of prominent types get in each other's way and the tempo drops, gifting a soft lead to Schrodinger's Cat.
scenarios.body: A fractured early order with no one willing to chase creates a dawdle and Schrodinger's Cat simply quickens away from minimal pressure; hold-up horses are stranded with nowhere to go and no pace to chase.

watchPoints.text: River Spey, Quantum Power, and One And Gone are all natural front-runners who cannot all find prominent ground in an 18-runner field — watch for early barging and interference in the first furlong as they jostle for position.|

Quantum Power has won three straight at Goodwood 5f and wears a visor — if David Egan manages to slot him close to the pace despite the redistribution, his course form makes him an immediate threat to any outcome.|

Old Is Gold returns after a 97-day absence — if Balding has had this Goodwood 5f course-winner tuned up quietly, the freshness could be dangerous, but the fitness question in a 18-runner sprint must be respected.|

U S S Charleston races just 6 days after its last run — monitor in the paddock for any signs of a hard race taking its toll, as the quick turnaround in a competitive handicap often catches horses out.|

The Good to Firm surface confirmed for the 4:10 is faster than the nominal Good card entry — horses who have an established record on firmer ground (Naana's Shadow, Miss Yechance, Dazzling Haze) gain a small structural edge over those with only soft-ground wins.|

races.name: Whispering Angel Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Shadow King
runners_data.note: Won at Goodwood over 6f on similar going, now steps up to 7f — the extra furlong looks within range for a horse that races prominently; Richard Hannon yard in solid nick (9/49 T14) and Sean Levey knows this track, making him a key hold-the-position rival to Cilician.
runners_data.comment: Shadow King arrives on the back of a win last time out, and a winner three starts back too, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour — the concern is whether seven days since that latest victory leaves him short of peak freshness.

runners_data.name: Cilician
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter who has been placed at this exact course and distance four times — his ability to control tempo from the front on Good to Firm Goodwood ground is the defining tactical factor of this race, even if his winning form is elusive.
runners_data.comment: Cilician has finished second three times in his last four starts, and at 135 lb from stall seven he arrives fresh on 13 days' rest with experience over today's trip and going — the main risk is that he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sword Salute
runners_data.note: Won over this exact trip at Goodwood earlier in the season and has strong course-and-distance credentials, though a 42-day absence and a 13th last time out at the same venue raises fitness and confidence questions for Charlie Johnston's runner.
runners_data.comment: Sword Salute won two starts back and was third three starts back, but comes here unplaced last time out and 42 days off; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 87 gives him claims, though the return from a break is the key question.

runners_data.name: My A'Ali Baba
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for David Evans on a horse that won over 6f on soft ground — the step up to 7f and quicker footing at Goodwood are both worth monitoring, having only run once on comparable going (unplaced).
runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back but has since found only third and fifth, giving him a mixed profile heading in here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 133 lb from stall nine rounds out a picture of a horse capable of better but needing to find it again.

runners_data.name: The Ginger Kid
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has already been placed at 7f at Goodwood; Kieran Shoemark is an astute tactical jockey who will need the pace to be sufficient to deliver this one, and Ed Walker's yard is firing (9/37 T14).
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and a winner three starts back, though unplaced on two occasions in between, The Ginger Kid has run over today's trip and going and arrives 20 days fresh with his trainer firing at 28% — 131 lb from stall 3 is the counter.

runners_data.name: The Bookkeeper
runners_data.note: Unresolved running style (U) makes race-reading difficult — Ryan Moore on a horse that won over 7f on soft with a 55-day break is interesting, but the lack of comparable going form and the prominent-heavy early fractions add uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back and looking well treated on official figures, The Bookkeeper carries a solid profile into this with distance and going experience to call on; the 55-day absence is the one query against him from stall two off 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Caeruleus
runners_data.note: Ran well to finish 1st at 6f at Sandown last time, stepping up in trip for John Butler; David Egan rides and the horse holds no Goodwood form — the combination of course debut and trip extension makes this a test of adaptability.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the field on our figures and drawn in stall 12, Caeruleus is hard to fancy at the weights carrying 130 lb, though he does bring a win in his last three starts and has run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Everatease
runners_data.note: Two consecutive wins at Goodwood over 6f on quick ground show genuine course aptitude; Charles Bishop rides for Eve Johnson Houghton's yard and the step to 7f is the primary unknown for a horse whose form is built on shorter, sharper speed.
runners_data.comment: Everatease comes here on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, so conditions shouldn't be an issue; the 48-day break is the one query, but he's got obvious recent momentum and 129 lb from stall 16 gives him a clear chance.

runners_data.name: Mia Fantasia
runners_data.note: Placed and won at this exact course and distance in her only two starts, giving her the cleanest Goodwood 7f profile in the field; Oisin Murphy picks up the ride for Hugo Palmer, whose yard has form (3/21 T14), making this a hard horse to dismiss.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out but a winner two starts back, Mia Fantasia arrives on a reasonable 19-day turnaround with experience over today's trip; carrying 128 lb from stall 13 leaves him with plenty to find against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Leave The Bag In
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has placed over 7f on soft — the quicker ground and front-controlled pace may not suit a horse that needs a searching gallop to arrive late; a 7lb claimer in Toby Moore is a negative in a competitive 18-runner nursery.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out but seventh and eighth in his two starts before that, Leave The Bag In arrives 49 days fresh and yet to win in recent starts; he has run over today's trip and going, but a rating of 81 and stall one leave him with plenty to prove from midfield.

runners_data.name: Agitator
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a material concern over a stiff Goodwood 7f that punishes those who cannot sustain their effort; won over 6f at Goodwood but that fade tendency reduces confidence in the step up.
runners_data.comment: Two unplaced efforts sandwiching a win make Agitator's form inconsistent, and ranked last on our figures he faces a stiff ask from stall 15 carrying 125 lb; experience over today's trip and going is the one positive to cling to.

runners_data.name: Cash Cove
runners_data.note: In reality a prominent racer who figures on the map in midfield only because the field is saturated with forward-going types — PJ McDonald will need early energy to recover a handy position, and the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 reflects that compromise.
runners_data.comment: Cash Cove showed her best two starts back when winning, though a third most recently suggests she's finding life tougher; she has run over today's trip and going before, but carrying 125 lb from stall 17 are factors to weigh against her.

runners_data.name: High Hazard
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with placed efforts at 8f and 7f at Goodwood, making this his home course; David Probert rides for Hugo Palmer and the horse needs the pace strong enough from Cilician to power through — that is the key dependency.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and second two starts back, High Hazard arrives in decent nick 26 days on; he has experience over today's trip and going, yet the 9th three starts back is a concern, and he remains winless in his last three runs.

runners_data.name: Rocket Boots
runners_data.note: Holds-up in rear and has only placed over 6f at Goodwood — the step to 7f is new territory and a 76-day break for James Owen's charge adds fitness doubt; needs the pace to be genuine to land a blow from off it.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and returning after 76 days off, Rocket Boot's ranking of 13th of 18 on our figures makes him hard to fancy, though a second two starts back and a trainer firing at 36% over the last fortnight offer slim crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Crazy Cubana
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer who is pushed back on the map by the congestion at the front — Ashley Lewis (5lb claim) will find it difficult to recover ideal position in an 18-runner field, and the STYLE_FIT discount is real and worth heeding.
runners_data.comment: Crazy Cubana showed real ability when winning three starts back, though she was unplaced two starts back before rallying to finish third last time out; she has run over today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 28% keeps her interesting, but stall 11 is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Wise And Wonderful
runners_data.note: Has already won over this trip at Goodwood and finished second here too — the course form is the best of the redistibuted trio; Saffie Osborne is capable of finding a positive position from the wide draw and the horse's natural style means it will want to be closer than the map implies.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14th of 18 on our figures and carrying 122 lb from stall 14, Wise And Wonderful faces a stiff task, though a win last time out and a trainer firing at 26% offer genuine encouragement; she has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Primal
runners_data.note: Unknown style (U) with modest recent form of 6-4-8 and no wins at Goodwood; Marco Ghiani takes the ride for Andrew Balding but the raw figures here are the least compelling in the field and there is little to anchor a positive case.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with an eighth last time out doing little to inspire confidence, Primal ranks 16th of 18 on our figures; the trainer's strong recent strike rate and experience over today's trip and going are the slender positives.

runners_data.name: Rbflying
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse that has been mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear — Duran Fentiman for Tim Easterby on a horse with limited form figures (6-5-3-7); the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.90 is the lowest in the field and the form does not offset the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 17th of 18 on our figures, Rbflying faces a stiff task here; a third two starts back offers a crumb of hope, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but the handicap weight of 121 lb from stall 10 adds to his burden.

races.paceDynamic: Cilician is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine rival willing to press for the lead — Shadow King, Sword Salute, My A'Ali Baba and Caeruleus are all prominent types but none is a natural pace-setter, meaning Cilician should control from the front at a rhythm entirely of Tom Marquand's choosing on Good to Firm ground over this stiff Goodwood 7f. The field is significantly overloaded with prominent-minded horses: Cash Cove, Wise And Wonderful and Crazy Cubana are all natural prominent racers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply no room for them at the front, and of those three Wise And Wonderful (Goodwood course winner, 7f form) is best-placed to recover a prominent berth with Saffie Osborne able to find cover. With Cilician able to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop rather than a searching pace, the 7f trip on quick ground will reward horses travelling smoothly in the first third and producing a controlled, progressive finish — true hold-up types who rely on a strong pace to bring them into the race are likely to find the tempo insufficient. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race within themselves just off the leader, travel into the race and quicken in the final two furlongs — a prominent-to-handy profile suits decisively.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cilician Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Cilician gets a clear, uncontested lead and Marquand controls tempo to suit a patient front-running display over this stiff 7f.
scenarios.body: Cilician settles into a comfortable rhythm with no rival willing to close the gap early, meaning the field never truly tests the pace; horses tracking within two lengths in a handy position get the softest possible run and have the tactical speed to respond when Marquand kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent-from-midfield horses — most likely Wise And Wonderful or Mia Fantasia — travels powerfully into the race and overpowers Cilician in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The compressed midfield bunch means a well-handicapped horse travelling smoothly can emerge from the pack with a clear run, and the stiff Goodwood finish rewards those who sustain their effort rather than sprint; Mia Fantasia's course-and-distance profile and Wise And Wonderful's previous Goodwood win make them the prime beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Thread Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated — perhaps Shadow King pushes Cilician — and the fractions become demanding enough for hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: The Ginger Kid and High Hazard both have genuine hold-up profiles with Goodwood form, and a genuinely run race at this trip on quick ground gives them the oxygen to find the line strongly; The Ginger Kid in particular has course form and was placed at 7f here already.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Undoes All
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so dawdling that the race becomes a sprint finish in the final two furlongs and luck-in-running becomes the dominant factor.
scenarios.body: A cavalry charge of 18 runners in a tight group on quick Goodwood ground creates positional chaos, and a horse drawn wide or deeply held up has almost no chance of threading through in time; this scenario is unlikely precisely because Cilician has every incentive to roll along rather than crawl.

watchPoints.text: Wise And Wonderful won over this exact trip at Goodwood and, despite being mapped to midfield due to field congestion, is a natural prominent racer — if Saffie Osborne can recover a position just off Cilician early, this horse's course-and-distance profile makes it a serious danger.
Mia Fantasia has placed and won in her only two starts both at Goodwood over 7f — a flawless course-and-distance record combined with an Oisin Murphy booking is a live danger flag in any conditions.

The cluster of redistributed prominent types — Cash Cove, Crazy Cubana and Wise And Wonderful — will all be competing for the same handy positions in the opening furlong of an 18-runner field; scrimmaging and interference are a real risk on the run down to the first bend.

Cilician has been placed four times at Goodwood without winning and carries the [STYLE_FIT=0.92] tag noting it may be racing out of role — if it fails to assert early or is pressured unexpectedly by Shadow King, the tactical premise of a controlled pace unravels.

The Ginger Kid and High Hazard are the two most credentialed hold-up types with genuine Goodwood 7f form — monitor whether the early pace from Cilician is brisk enough to bring them into contention in the final quarter-mile, as a slow gallop would strand both.

races.name: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
HKJC World Pool Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Intense Vision
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Oli Rix who hasn't run in 42 days; finished a creditable 20th of 20 on this course last time and is 0W0P in similar going — needs a truly strong pace to unlock his late run and that may not materialise here.
runners_data.comment: Showed a smart vein of form with back-to-back wins three and four starts back, but he disappointed last time out and the 42-day break adds a fitness query; has run over today's trip and carries 135 lb from stall 16.

runners_data.name: Exclusive Code
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field, James Doyle aboard for Archie Watson who is 1/13 in 14 days; won over this exact course and distance last time out, sits in his natural role and controls the tempo — the key pace-setter the entire race revolves around.
runners_data.comment: Exclusive Code won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with our rating putting him right in contention from stall one; the worry is that unplaced return last time out, now 42 days ago.

runners_data.name: Vincenzo Peruggia
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston runner — one of only two pure hold-up horses in the field; placed at Goodwood over course and distance and has winning form over a mile, but is 0 from 4 in similar going and needs an unusually strong pace in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Ran unplaced last time but boasts a second three starts back and a win five starts back, giving him something to build on; experience over today's trip and going helps, though 42 days off and a tough 134 lb ask make this a stern test.

runners_data.name: Wild Thoughts
runners_data.note: Six-race winning streak from Richard Spencer's yard with Saffie Osborne, including two wins over this course and distance; high-class prominent performer in excellent form and the [hg:p] headgear flags a switch that has coincided with this run of results — solid claims here racing in role.
runners_data.comment: Wild Thoughts won four of his last six starts but has drifted to seventh last time out, casting doubt on current form; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 134 lb is a significant burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Richie's Rocket
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's prominent type hasn't won in five starts, a string of placed efforts rather than victories (0W1P in similar going); Hector Crouch rides and the horse has consistent Goodwood course form but may lack that final gear to win a race of this depth.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Richie's Rocket nonetheless catches the eye on our rating of 102, and having run over today's trip and going before, he arrives fit on 26 days' rest — the one to side with here.

runners_data.name: Law Court
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's consistent performer placed five times in six recent starts including winning form over this mile trip; Faleh Bughanaim up and course and distance form is excellent — thrives prominent and this scenario suits if pace is controlled.
runners_data.comment: Law Court has been consistently in the thick of things, finishing second last time out and a winner two starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — the main query is whether 47 days off the track has left him short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Zennor Storm
runners_data.note: William Haggas's 3yo comes off a pair of wins earlier this season but has returned 4th and 10th at Goodwood on the last two tries; Tom Marquand rides, the headgear flag is noted, and reverting to the course where he won may help, though recent Goodwood form is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Zennor Storm showed his best form with back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and going; our rating of 96 suggests he retains ability, but a fourth last time out and a 132 lb burden from stall 13 are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Runswick
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's horse carries excellent recent form — won and placed over this mile trip; Daniel Tudhope rides and course wins are on his record, though soft-ground efforts outnumber fast-ground wins in the history and Good to Firm may stretch him slightly.
runners_data.comment: Runswick won last time out and was third three starts back, showing consistent recent form, but he faces a stiff ask from stall 19 carrying 132 lb off an official mark of 87 — experience over today's trip and going at least counts in his favour.

runners_data.name: Electric Dreams
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's lightly-raced 3yo — only three career runs — won over this exact track and trip last time; Oisin Murphy takes the ride and that combination of course-and-distance form plus a top jockey and upside makes this one interesting.
runners_data.comment: Electric Dreams won last time out but that victory came 47 days ago, he ranks a lowly 17th of 20 on our figures, and a speed rating of 70 makes him hard to fancy despite having experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Euston Hall
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3yo has won twice at this course and distance and arrives with two consecutive wins; Colin Keane takes over and the horse races prominently in his natural position — strong course claims and in-form profile.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into sixth last time out after back-to-back wins earlier in his recent form, Euston Hall returns after 41 days and faces a stiff task ranked 15th of 20 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going, and the trainer's 28% strike rate offers some hope.

runners_data.name: Go Rimbaud
runners_data.note: Buick and Gosden partnership brings class — the horse has winning and placed form on fast ground at Sandown and Yarmouth; naturally a prominent racer but the congested field means he may not secure his preferred position despite Buick's ability to manoeuvre early.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's trip, but Go Rimbaud's fifth two starts back tempers enthusiasm slightly; drawn in stall 15 carrying 130 lb, he has ability on his day yet consistency remains the question at this level.

runners_data.name: Storming Point
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore's booking is notable for Gary & Josh Moore's 3yo who has a consistent placed record (0W1P in similar going) but has yet to win; his natural style is to race prominently but the sheer volume of similar types means he'll likely be shuffled wider or deeper than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts despite a string of placed efforts, Storming Point has run over today's trip and returns after 30 days, but carrying 130 lb from stall 20 with our rating six pounds below his official mark makes him hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Abundant
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's 3yo races in his element when handy but is genuinely unlikely to find his preferred position in this traffic; recent form at Goodwood shows three placed efforts but no win in similar going, and being pushed out of his natural role is a real disadvantage here.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without quite winning, Abundant has been third twice in his last two starts and a winner four starts back, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; the 125 lb burden and draw 17 are the obvious counterweights to a timely 20-day break.

runners_data.name: Kalokalo
runners_data.note: Charles Hills's 3yo has winning form at the mile-and-a-quarter trip and a strong placed record; naturally races prominently but the overloaded pace map means Jason Watson will need to find a gap — distance may also be on the sharp side coming back from 10f.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 16 of 20 on our figures, Kalokalo faces a stiff ask at the bottom of the assessments, and a speed rating of 69 does little to inspire confidence — yet he does arrive in decent nick, third last time out after winning two starts back, with distance and going experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: Loblolly
runners_data.note: David Egan and S Woods combine with a hold-up type who has placed consistently over 8-10f at Goodwood; 0W2P in similar going and needs the pace to stack up, but is at least racing in an authentic style for this shape — one of the few genuine closers.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Loblolly does bring experience over today's trip and going, and consecutive thirds suggest a degree of consistency — but his ranking of 14th in the field and a speed rating of 75 leave him with plenty to find against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Get Outta Here
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's 3yo has solid placed form at Goodwood in similar going and won over this course; Jamie Spencer typically finds cover late, but the horse's natural style is forward-going and being pushed into mid-division dilutes his chance.
