runners_data.comment: Get Outta Here arrives in fair nick — placed last time out and a winner three starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, though our rating of 88 suggests he may face stiffer competition than his official mark of 79 implies.

runners_data.name: Aqua Bear
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's 3yo has a win at seven furlongs and placed efforts at Goodwood; Billy Loughnane rides, but the horse's tendency to race prominently will be frustrated by the crowded early stages and dropping him back is not his preferred mode.
runners_data.comment: Aqua Bear has experience of today's trip and conditions, and his third two starts back shows he can get into the mix, but unplaced runs either side of that effort are a concern; 124 lb from stall 18 adds to the task.

runners_data.name: Dumuji
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's 3yo hasn't run in 80 days — notable freshness angle — and won last time at Sandown; P J McDonald rides but the lengthy absence, combined with the horse's natural prominent style being squeezed out of that position, makes this a difficult task on return.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in his last two starts and returning after 80 days off, Dumuji is a difficult proposition ranked 18th of 20 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, and his win three starts back offers the one crumb of hope.

runners_data.name: Storm Point
runners_data.note: Ed Walker double (with Euston Hall) — Kieran Shoemark up for a 3yo who won over a mile on soft ground; the horse's natural style is to race prominently but fast ground is a potential concern (1/7 in similar going) and the crowded midfield map does not play to his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Storm Point has looked inconsistent in recent starts — seventh last time out and sixth three starts back undermine two wins in his last five — and he ranks last on our figures, with a speed rating of 65 doing him no favours. A firing trainer and experience over today's trip offer slim reasons for hope.

runners_data.name: Mr Seagull
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's 3yo carries recent form with a fifth at Goodwood over this trip; David Probert rides and the horse has placed on Good to Firm but has a wide draw and is naturally prominent — the overcrowded pace map means [hg:p] headgear must produce a career best from a difficult position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Mr Seagull has at least been running consistently around the midfield placings, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 122 lb from stall 12, his rating of 92 suggests he holds claims, though his recent record offers little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Exclusive Code is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 20-runner field and, with no natural rival for the early lead, should stride clear to set a controlled, uncrowded tempo on Good to Firm ground at Goodwood's mile. Behind him, a mass of genuine prominent-types — Wild Thoughts, Richie's Rocket, Law Court, Zennor Storm, Runswick, Electric Dreams and Euston Hall — will contest the next tier aggressively, creating a compressed prominent group rather than a settled midfield, and that bunching will burn energy from horses who would prefer to be handier. The field holds considerably more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Go Rimbaud, Storming Point, Abundant, Kalokalo, Get Outta Here, Aqua Bear, Dumuji, Storm Point and Mr Seagull are all naturally prominent but cannot all hold that position, with Go Rimbaud (Buick/Gosden) and Storming Point (Ryan Moore) best-placed by jockey seniority to push forward and actually secure a spot near the pace. Sustainable early fractions set by Exclusive Code on fast ground over a flat mile suits horses who can travel smoothly in the prominent-to-midfield tier and produce a clean, sustained late run — the pace profile clearly advantages prominent horses and genuine hold-up closers who save ground and peak in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Exclusive Code Controls; Closers Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If Exclusive Code dictates a steady-to-moderate tempo unchallenged, luring the prominent pack into a falsely-run dash that burns off those who over-race.
scenarios.body: Exclusive Code sets fractions that keep the race controlled until the straight, where the stamina-laden hold-up horses arriving fresh from behind carve through a tiring prominent pack; the genuine one-mile specialists with clean action on fast ground who travel well off a strong pace-setter's rhythm are rewarded.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate; Track Bias
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed prominent group behind Exclusive Code travels efficiently and the Good to Firm surface rewards those who race handy throughout.
scenarios.body: With no true pace injection to stretch the field, the horses racing in positions three to eight through the first half of the race save ground, avoid traffic, and have enough left to sustain their run through the Goodwood straight; genuine one-mile performers who can hold a prominent position despite the congestion are best served.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses; Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group is slow to organise behind Exclusive Code and the early pace proves genuinely slow, allowing Exclusive Code to steal a march turning in.
scenarios.body: With a truly unchallenged lead and the field's attention split among jostling rivals, Exclusive Code converts his solo role into a front-running success on ground that suits quick-actioned horses; his Goodwood form and course familiarity add credibility.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Strong Pace; Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack accelerates hard early in pursuit of Exclusive Code, creating genuine pace that sets up a late rush from genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A truly contested gallop would bring Intense Vision and Vincenzo Peruggia — the two authentic hold-up horses — into the picture late, though with only 20 runners and limited genuine closers this scenario requires near-perfect pace conditions and clear runs that are far from guaranteed.

watchPoints.text: Exclusive Code (James Doyle) is the lone front-runner in 20 — watch how quickly he's allowed to go clear at the start, as any stumble or slow break could see Go Rimbaud or Storming Point steal his position before he can establish.

The section from stalls to the first furlong will be chaotic — with nine genuinely prominent-natured horses fighting for four or five positions, watch for bumping, checking and horses immediately racing wider than ideal, particularly affecting Storming Point, Abundant and Aqua Bear.

Wild Thoughts carries [hg:p] headgear and a six-race winning streak — if she travels strongly and over-races in the prominent group trying to be near Exclusive Code, she risks burning her finishing kick before the straight.

Electric Dreams (Oisin Murphy) is lightly raced with only three runs — the 47-day absence and small sample of form means she could improve dramatically or find the big-field dynamics completely different from her previous controlled race contexts.

Track position at Goodwood's mile start on Good to Firm is historically significant — horses drawn wider often get shuffled back early; watch which of the redistributed prominent types (Go Rimbaud, Storming Point) manage to hold a forward pitch versus those who drop to genuine midfield.
